title: Ternary codimension-six LCD distance-four exceptions
summary: Decide whether ternary Euclidean LCD codes of codimension six and minimum distance four exist at each of six residual lengths.

formal_statement.body: For every $n\in\{51,52,53,54,55,56\}$, decide whether a ternary Euclidean LCD code with parameters $[n,n-6,4]$ exists. Equivalently, determine whether $d_3^E(n,n-6)=4$ or $d_3^E(n,n-6)=3$ for each of these six lengths.

scope.domain: Ternary Euclidean linear complementary dual codes of codimension six
assumptions: The TIT source already bounds the optimum minimum distance to either 3 or 4 at every listed length
scope.unresolved_remainder: All six instances remain open. Later inspected ternary LCD tables stop at length 50 and do not construct or rule out any of $[51,45,4]$, $[52,46,4]$, $[53,47,4]$, $[54,48,4]$, $[55,49,4]$, or $[56,50,4]$.

progress.summary: The TIT source isolates six ternary codimension-six lengths where the optimum minimum distance remains either 3 or 4.
